definitions.explanation: Used to describe doing something with urgency or speed. The te-form of the verb {急|いそ}ぐ (to hurry), functioning as an adverb.

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}いで{朝|あさ}ごはんを{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate breakfast in a hurry.

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}いで{準備|じゅんび}しないと{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れるよ。
examples.english: If you don't get ready quickly, you'll miss the train.

notes:
The te-form of {急|いそ}ぐ (to hurry), used adverbially to modify the action that follows. It conveys a sense of urgency — that something is being done faster than usual, often because of time pressure.

USAGE:
Placed before the main verb to indicate the manner of the action. Often used in commands or suggestions when time is short.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {急|いそ}いで{行|い}く — to go in a hurry
- {急|いそ}いで{食|た}べる — to eat quickly
- {急|いそ}いで{準備|じゅんび}する — to prepare in a rush
- {急|いそ}いで{帰|かえ}る — to hurry home

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {慌|あわ}てて — in a fluster, in a panic; implies more disorganization than {急|いそ}いで
- {大急|おおいそ}ぎで — in a great hurry; stronger emphasis on urgency
